questions.question: You are at a formal meeting and a colleague makes a mistake in the presentation. What is the most appropriate way to point out the error?
options: That was a terrible mistake you made.
I think you might have forgotten to include that data point.
You should have checked your notes before starting.
This is completely wrong and you need to fix it now.
questions.answer: I think you might have forgotten to include that data point.

questions.question: A friend asks for a lift home, but you are already driving to work and have a full car. How do you respond?
options: Sure, get in. It's no trouble.
I'd love to give you a lift, but I'm already heading to work.
Why didn't you take the bus earlier?
I can drop you off at the station on my way back.
questions.answer: I'd love to give you a lift, but I'm already heading to work.

questions.question: During a debate, a classmate argues strongly against your view. How do you respond to disagree politely?
options: You are absolutely wrong about that.
I see your point, but I believe there is more evidence to support my side.
That is the only logical conclusion.
I agree with you completely.
questions.answer: I see your point, but I believe there is more evidence to support my side.

questions.question: You are at a party and someone offers you a drink. You are not feeling well and do not wish to drink alcohol. What is the best response?
options: Thanks, I'll have a beer.
I'm not feeling very well today, so I'd prefer not to drink.
That's a good idea, but I'm too busy.
Sure, just one.
questions.answer: I'm not feeling very well today, so I'd prefer not to drink.

questions.question: You are asking a stranger for directions to a specific shop in a large city. Which response is the most helpful and polite?
options: Go straight and turn left.
I don't know where that is.
You should use Google Maps.
It's too far to walk.
